additional_priorities.quote: If an individual is a dependent of a taxpayer for any taxable year of such taxpayer beginning in a calendar year, such individual shall be treated as having no dependents for any taxable year of such individual beginning in such calendar year.

other_issues: Rule transferred63c5 and predicate section_63_c_5_applies are unsupported by the supplied TRAIN statutes, which contain only sections 151 and 152.
The shared ?year argument in the section 152(b)(1) rules conflates potentially distinct taxable years that merely begin in the same calendar year.

The shared ?year argument in the section 151(d)(2) rules likewise conflates the other taxpayer's taxable year with the individual's taxable year, although the statute requires only that they begin in the same calendar year.

r151_c_deduction_allowable attributes deduction allowability directly to section 151(c), whereas section 151(c) provides the dependent exemption and section 151(a) supplies the rule that exemptions are allowed as deductions.
value.source_review: Yes. Section 152(b)(1) is an express exception requiring the negative dependent conclusion to defeat an otherwise inferred positive dependent relation for the individual, possible dependent, and relevant calendar year.
